Article Title: Canada government warns country's largest financial institutions and banks on Anthropic's Claude Mythos and other AI models; says: New technology can ...
Article Text:
Global concerns over Mythos



Banks respond with AI defenses



Government access and industry impact



Anthropic just made an admission on Claude that may scare many of companies



Canada’s federal banking regulator has warned the country’s largest financial institutions about the risks posed by Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and other advanced AI systems, according to a report by Reuters. In an April email obtained by Reuters, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) cautioned that frontier AI models could increase cyber threats and compress the time banks have to identify and fix the vulnerabilities. The email, sent to chief technology, information security, and risk officers across Canada’s financial industry, outlined practices to enhance risk identification and response. “Advanced artificial intelligence models, such as Anthropic Claude Mythos, significantly compress the timeframe for effective risk mitigation,” OSFI wrote.Following Reuters’ inquiries, OSFI published a public bulletin emphasising its technology-neutral, risk-focused approach. The regulator said its concern is not the technology itself but how institutions govern and manage risks associated with its use.Cybersecurity experts have described Mythos as extremely capable at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, raising alarms for legacy banking systems. The warning comes after U.S. regulators, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and then-Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, convened urgent meetings with bank CEOs earlier this year to discuss similar risks.Canada’s big six banks — Royal Bank of Canada, TD Bank, BMO, Scotiabank, CIBC, and National Bank — have all disclosed AI initiatives ranging from chatbots to internal tools. RBC’s AI Group Head Bruce Ross said Mythos underscores a shift in the cyberattack landscape: “The way we’re dealing with it is building our own AI defenses… we’ll continue to do that.”The Canadian government has said it has access to Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, which enables companies to use Mythos, though it remains unclear which banks are deploying it. The Canadian Bankers Association noted that institutions have invested heavily in cybersecurity and comply with OSFI’s robust requirements for risk management and incident reporting.Recently, Anthropic revealed that its AI model Claude uses a small enterable workspace to hold and manipulate ideas without expressing them in words. The said that this structure, dubbed ‘J-Space’, shows intriguing similarities to how humans consciously access thoughts. According to a report by Axios, in a video demonstration, Anthropic explained, “We can see Claude silently perform reasoning steps in its head—noticing bugs in code, identifying images, and more. ” The J-Space operates separately from the “chain of thought” reasoning Claude shares with users, allowing the model to plan strategies unrelated to its immediate task.Anthropic’s findings also highlight a division between deliberate reasoning and the larger volume of automatic computation beneath it. In the research paper the company used a word “conscious” more than 200 times, though it stopped short of claiming Claude is conscious. The discovery adds fuel to ongoing debates over machine consciousness and whether advanced AI systems are approaching AGI.
Article Summary: Canada’s federal banking regulator has warned banks about the risks posed by advanced AI systems. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) cautioned that frontier AI models could increase cyber threats and compress the time banks have to identify and fix the vulnerabilities.

Article Title: Telling Apple employees coming for job interviews to bring in CAD designs; stealing laptops and other 'explosive' claims made in Apple's 41-page lawsuit against ChatGPT maker OpenAI
Article Text:
Coaching job candidates to bring CAD designs

The alleged case of coordinated misconduct

A partnership that turned into rivalry

What OpenAI said about these allegations

Apple has filed a 41-page lawsuit against ChatGPT-maker OpenAI, accusing the AI giant of orchestrating a corporate espionage campaign through former Apple employees. The case revolves around Tang Yew Tan and Chang Liu, whom Apple claims engaged in a ‘pattern theft’ of trade secrets and some of the ‘most valuable intellectual assets in all of American business’. According to a report by Fortune, Apple alleges that Chang Liu, a former senior system electrical engineer, failed to return a company-issued laptop and also exploited a rare authentication bug to access Apple’s internal network. As per the suit filed, Liu messaged colleague Alyssa Peng: “LOL, I found out I can access the [network storage], so funny.” He then downloaded dozens of confidential files, including unreleased product designs and engineering presentations.The lawsuit also accuses Tang Yew Tan, Apple’s former iPhone and Apple Watch design chief, of using the job internees at OpenAI to mine information from present Apple employees. The Cupertino-based tech giant claims that Tan asked candidates to bring CAD designs and prototypes and also divulge the details of the suppliers. One employee was reportedly shocked, saying he ‘didn’t even know we could take those from the office.Apple further argues that these actions reflect a ‘coordinated pattern of misconduct at an institutional level’ within OpenAI. The company also claims that OpenAI has contacted Apple’s suppliers in order to replicate proprietary manufacturing techniques, misleading them into believing that Apple has authorised the work.Apple entered into a partnership with OpenAI in 2024. As part of the association Apple was to integrate ChatGPT into Siri but later it switched to Google Gemini in January 2026. This lawsuit filed by Apple marks a dramatic escalation in tensions, with Apple now accusing OpenAI of systematically raiding its talent pool — more than 400 ex-Apple employees have joined OpenAI — and misappropriating trade secrets to build an AI-powered hardware device.OpenAI told Fortune it has “no interest in other companies’ trade secrets” and is reviewing the lawsuit. “We remain focused on building innovative technology that empowers people everywhere,” the company said.
Article Summary: Apple has filed a 41-page lawsuit against ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. The tech giant accuses the AI giant of orchestrating a corporate espionage campaign through former Apple employees. The case revolves around Tang Yew Tan and Chang Liu, whom Apple claims engaged in a ‘pattern theft’ of trade secrets.

Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos’ wife Lauren Sanchez

Quote of the day by Lauren Sanchez Bezos

"I want to be in a helicopter all the time. Life can be so chaotic with so much going on. Lift off, and you're in an energy space that no one else is in. It's calming"

Lauren Sanchez Bezos’ quote meaning explained

Why flying became more than a job for her

Why everyone benefits from a place to disconnect

Perspective shifts once you rise above the immediate problem

Other memorable quotes by Lauren Sanchez Bezos

"I loved being on camera. And now, I still have a camera. It's just 3,000 feet in the air."

"When I first became a reporter, I did it because there was no one else I thought that looked like me."

"There's a special kind of trust that comes when you watch your kid take off on their own for the first time. It's about letting go, but also knowing they're more than ready."

"It was an incredible experience because I think only 3% of helicopter pilots were women at the time. Now I think it's about 6%."

What it means in today's world

Most people look for stillness somewhere quiet, a walk, a book, a few minutes of silence. Lauren Sanchez , the journalist turned licensed helicopter pilot, finds hers thousands of feet above the ground. "I want to be in a helicopter all the time," she has said. "Life can be so chaotic with so much going on. Lift off, and you're in an energy space that no one else is in. It's calming." It is an unusual place to look for peace, though for someone who built an entire second career around flying, it makes a certain kind of sense. Most people have to actively carve out space away from the noise. She found hers by learning an entirely new skill from scratch and turning it into a genuine second profession.The quote starts with something personal, a feeling that everyday life rarely provides. "Life can be so chaotic with so much going on" names the constant pull of responsibilities and interruptions that most people recognise instantly. The helicopter, in her description, is not really about transportation. It becomes a place where that noise temporarily disappears.The phrase "an energy space that no one else is in" is doing the real work here.It is describing a mental state as much as a physical one, a pocket of focus and clarity that outside pressure cannot reach. The quote is really an invitation to find your own version of that space, whatever shape it happens to take.Sanchez built an unusually varied career, working for years as an Emmy-winning television journalist before training as a helicopter pilot, a pursuit she has said she took up in her forties after growing up around aviation, since her parents ran a flight school. She has spoken about the specific challenge of getting her licence while managing dyslexia, describing the process as difficult enough that she cried working through it.That effort eventually led her to found Black Ops Aviation, an aerial film company, at a time when only around three per cent of helicopter pilots were women. Flying, for her, became a skill built from real, sustained effort rather than a passing interest, which is part of why the calm she describes in the cockpit carries weight beyond a nice turn of phrase.Most people will never fly a helicopter, but the underlying idea travels well beyond aviation. Everyone benefits from some space that creates real distance from routine pressure, a walk, a hobby, an hour with no phone nearby. The specific activity matters less than what it does for the mind, giving it room to pause and come back with more clarity than it had before.Problems tend to look larger at ground level than they do from a distance. Stepping back from a stressful situation, literally or otherwise, tends to make it easier to judge clearly rather than react to it in the moment. That is really what the image of lifting off is doing in the quote, offering a physical version of the emotional distance that clear thinking usually requires.Constant notifications and endless small demands make genuine stillness harder to find than it has probably ever been. Sanchez's quote is a reminder that everyone needs some version of that stillness, whether that happens to be a cockpit, a quiet trail, or simply a few uninterrupted minutes with a book. The setting matters less than the space it actually creates. the main factor being the growth of the demand that played a small role. The detail that makes the quote more than a lifestyle observation is the work behind it: a licence earned while managing dyslexia, at a time when three percent of helicopter pilots were women, resulting in an actual second career rather than a hobby. The calm she describes in the cockpit was purchased with genuine difficulty, which is probably part of why it feels so different from the noise below.
Article Summary: Lauren Sanchez Bezos is the wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos. She is a licensed helicopter pilot and former television journalist. The quote of the day is about finding stillness in the cockpit. It is an invitation to find your own version of that space, whatever it takes.

Article Title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp says AI may be creating ‘America's biggest problem’ by making …
Article Text:
Alex Karp: AI is creating a 'complete decoupling' of wealth

Palantir CEO Alex Karp recently warned that AI is creating a widening wealth gap, with the biggest gains going to those developing the technology. Speaking in an interview with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner, Karp said this growing inequality is the "biggest problem" in the United States and added that AI is being oversold, as not everyone will benefit equally from the technology despite its potential to improve lives. "While it will raise the standard of living of the average person, the people involved are likely to get 10, 100 times wealthier than they already are," Alex Karp said. He further stated that this AI wealth disparity is the "biggest problem in this country."Alex Karp also criticised how AI is being promoted. “The overselling of AI in this country is really, really, really, somewhat disconcerting, but it's also depressing because you don't have to do it,” he said, describing AI as a “natural resource” with both positive and negative potential.During the interview, Alex Karp said earlier technological revolutions also created wealth, but the gap between the richest people and everyone else was much smaller. “The person at the bottom, maybe their salary doubled, and the person at the top became five times wealthier, but it was very unusual to be a billionaire 40 years ago,” Karp said.He further added: “You now have a revolution where, you know, I could become 20 times wealthier than I am now.”Alex Karp said AI is creating a “complete decoupling” between ordinary economic gains and a small group of people who achieve "unimaginable wealth." He also said many people worry about AI because some of the industry's leading figures have warned that the technology could disrupt jobs.“The people running the lab companies, who are the leaders, told you it's true,” Alex Karp said. “They're telling you your life is going to suck. And they're also getting very wealthy, and you don't find them very likable.”While Karp did not name anyone, executives including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have previously warned that AI could disrupt jobs, though both have recently softened their comments.He also took a swipe at some of the people leading the AI industry. “These are like very oddly-shaped-IQ specimens that you probably wouldn't want to have over for dinner,” Karp said. “And if they were over for the dinner, you have nothing to talk to them about. And, by the way, vice versa.”
Article Summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp said AI is creating a 'complete decoupling' of wealth. He said the biggest gains are going to those developing the technology. Karp also criticised how AI is being promoted in the U.S.

Article Title: OnePlus may shut down in US, Europe within days; parent company Oppo to take over
Article Text:
OnePlus is reportedly exiting the US and Europe, with India left as the brand's biggest surviving market.

What happens to your OnePlus phone if the brand exits

The signs OnePlus was winding down have been piling up all year

OnePlus, the brand that once sold flagship specs at half the price and dared everyone else to keep up, is reportedly about to stop selling phones in the US and Europe altogether. German outlet WinFuture, citing well-informed sources, reports that OnePlus and parent company Oppo will announce "fundamental changes" to their strategy in the coming days—corporate language that, in practice, means a full withdrawal from two of the brand's most visible markets.Closed-door press briefings have already happened, according to the report, though company representatives apparently declined to explain why the brand is being pulled. India and China were left conspicuously unaddressed too. The expectation is that OnePlus continues in both as a product line inside Oppo—cheaper phones, tablets, no independent identity. India is the reason it survives at all. The country accounts for well over half of OnePlus's annual sales, and the Nord series still sells hard in the mid-range.Existing owners aren't being cut loose immediately. OnePlus and Oppo told the press that software updates and after-sales support will continue for already-sold devices until the end of their respective lifecycles. What ends is everything ahead of that—no new launches, no fresh stock, no local marketing. Remaining inventory in Europe and the US is being sold off over the coming weeks and months, and OnePlus's European online stores are already close to empty.None of this arrives out of nowhere. Android Headlines reported in January that OnePlus was being dismantled; the company denied it. 9to5Google reported in March that operations could cease in global markets as early as April. India CEO Robin Liu left the same month. By April, OnePlus admitted it was "evaluating its regional roadmap and product strategy" in Europe. Then came the reported Realme merger, the Smartprix report that OxygenOS would be folded into ColorOS, and finally OnePlus's own websites in Germany, Spain and France running banners pushing shoppers towards Oppo instead.Oppo will move into the space OnePlus leaves behind in Europe. There is an obvious flaw in that plan: Oppo phones cost more. You cannot fill a value-brand hole with a premium lineup and expect nobody to notice. Nothing is official until Oppo says it is—but the OnePlus 15 now looks like the brand's last major Western release, and a five-star one at that.
Article Summary: OnePlus is reportedly exiting the US and Europe, with India left as the brand's biggest surviving market. India accounts for well over half of OnePlus's annual sales, and the Nord series still sells hard in the mid-range. Remaining inventory in Europe and the US is being sold off.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs has a new rule for its employees: They are now banned from trading on…
Article Text:
Why prediction markets are giving compliance teams a headache



Goldman is stricter than its rivals, but not the strictest on the Street



Goldman Sachs has told its employees to stay away from prediction markets, unless the bet in question involves a football match or a reality show finale. The Wall Street bank recently updated its personal trading policy to prohibit employees from trading event contracts tied to specific companies, election outcomes, or the performance of any financial market. That covers Goldman's own stock, ceasefire dates in ongoing conflicts, the price of Bitcoin, and even whether a merger clears regulatory approval. The rules come with teeth. Repeated violations can lead to termination or the closure of a staff member's trading account. If a banned trade goes through and turns a profit above $200, Goldman can make the employee forfeit the money or donate it to charity. Betting on whether a team wins a championship, though, is still fine. Goldman declined to comment on the policy, which was first reported by Bloomberg.Kalshi and Polymarket have exploded over the past year, letting anyone wager on everything from elections to corporate earnings to where the S&P 500 lands on a given day. Kalshi is reportedly in talks to raise money at a valuation of roughly $40 billion. But the same platforms have been repeatedly jolted by people who seemed to know something before everyone else did.A US special forces soldier with advance knowledge of the operation to capture Nicolás Maduro allegedly placed bets on it on Polymarket. Nobel Peace Prize organisers looked into a possible leak after a rush of successful bets landed on the eventual Venezuelan winner. The Financial Times separately flagged 12 suspicious accounts that made unusually well-timed, high-value bets days before the initial US strike on Iran this year. For a bank whose employees routinely handle material non-public information, that is an obvious problem.JPMorgan Chase took a softer line, telling staff to "think carefully" before participating in markets linked to the financial sector. Morgan Stanley says it has rules but won't detail them. Bank of America restricts company-specific, macroeconomic and financial services contracts, and confirmed it recently updated its guidance with clearer examples.Hedge funds have gone further. Point72 and Balyasny have imposed blanket bans on personal prediction market accounts.The irony is that Wall Street still wants the business. CEO David Solomon called the platforms "super interesting" in January and said he had met leaders of both major firms. Susquehanna and Jump Trading are already making markets on the exchanges.
Article Summary: Goldman Sachs has updated its personal trading policy to prohibit employees from trading event contracts tied to specific companies, election outcomes, or the performance of any financial market. Repeated violations can lead to termination or the closure of a staff member's trading account. Betting on whether a team wins a championship is still fine.

Article Title: Former FTC chairman Lina Khan, who many CEOs in Silicon Valley said went too far, sends a thanks note to Zohran Mamdani for bringing what she ...
Article Text:
What is Zohran Mamdani's 'Click-to-Cancel' rule



Former FTC chairman Lina Khan has sent a thanks note to Mayor Zohran Mamdani for 'Click-to-Cancel' rule he announced recently. New York will become the first city in the US to require that consumers be allowed to cancel subscriptions for streaming services, gym memberships and more in the way that they signed up. FTC's ex-chairman Lina Khan commended Mamdani for the same. "Thanks to Mayor Mamdani’s administration, businesses must now make it as easy to cancel a subscription as it is to sign up for one. New Yorkers can report subscription tricks and traps by calling 311 or filing a complaint at http://nyc.gov/consumer," she wrote.Lina Khan was made the head of FTC in 2021 by the former US President Joe Biden. During her four-year tenure she had many fights with technology companies including Amazon, Google, Meta and Nvidia. In Silicon Valley, many industry leaders are of the view that she went too far. There were reported to be significant courtroom victories under her, including the block on Kroger’s $25 billion merger with Albertsons. The chip giant Nvidia reportedly abandoned its $40 billion bid for Arm, after the FTC sued to block the deal. There were also losses, such as FTC's failed bid to block Microsoft’s $69 billion (£57bn) deal to buy Activision Blizzard, publisher of mega gaming franchises including Call of Duty, World of Warcraft and Candy Crush.Incidentally, in March 2023, FTC announced a proposed “click to cancel” provision requiring sellers to make it as easy for consumers to cancel their enrollment as it was to sign up. That is just one of several significant updates the Commission is proposing to its rules regarding subscriptions and recurring payments. The new click to cancel provision, along with other proposals, would go a long way to rescuing consumers from seemingly never-ending struggles to cancel unwanted subscription payment plans for everything from cosmetics to newspapers to gym memberships.“Some businesses too often trick consumers into paying for subscriptions they no longer want or didn’t sign up for in the first place,” said FTC's then-Chair Lina Khan. She added, “The proposed rule would require that companies make it as easy to cancel a subscription as it is to sign up for one. The proposal would save consumers time and money, and businesses that continued to use subscription tricks and traps would be subject to stiff penalties. ”The notice of proposed rulemaking announced was part of the FTC’s ongoing review of its 1973 Negative Option Rule, which the agency uses to combat unfair or deceptive practices related to subscriptions, memberships, and other recurring-payment programs.New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) Commissioner Samuel A.A. Levine announced new consumer protections that will crack down on junk fees and subscription traps, making it easier for New Yorkers to know the real price of what they are buying and to stop paying for the services they no longer want.Following Mayor Mamdani’s Executive Orders 9 and 10, the City announced a proposed rule requiring transparent, all-in pricing that bans hidden junk fees, alongside a final “Click to Cancel” rule that guarantees consumers can cancel subscriptions as easily as they sign up for them.Together, these rules represent one of the strongest municipal consumer protection efforts in the country and build upon Mayor Mamdani’s affordability agenda, including the City’s rule banning hidden hotel fees. The Click-to-Cancel Rule alone is estimated to save New Yorkers up to $162.5 million per year.“For years, companies have built their business model around making it harder for working people to hold onto their money,” said Mayor Mamdani. “Whether it’s hidden fees that suddenly appear at checkout or subscriptions that take one click to sign up for and a dozen steps to cancel, the result is the same: working people pay more while corporations profit. That ends now. If you can sign up with one click, you can cancel with one click. ”“Every dollar a family loses to a hidden fee or a subscription they couldn’t cancel is a dollar stolen from them, a dollar that could have gone toward rent, groceries, childcare, or anything else. And just as important, the hours spent trying to cancel a subscription or membership you no longer want is stolen time,” said Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su. “That’s what affordability means in practice—closing the small holes that drain people’s paychecks and their time month after month. These rules put New Yorkers back in control.”“The Mamdani Administration is shutting the door on the era of fleecing New Yorkers with junk fees and subscription traps,” said Commissioner Samuel A.A. Levine. “These two rules will ensure that the price you see is the price you pay—no hidden charges, no endless subscription services and no advantages for businesses that cheat. Requiring companies to compete on price will lower costs for all New Yorkers and level the playing field for honest businesses. ”“Nobody should be trapped in subscriptions they can’t escape or stuck paying junk fees they can’t avoid,” said Lina Khan, former FTC Chair. “These predatory tactics cheat people out of billions of dollars each year. With today’s rules, Commissioner Levine and DCWP are cracking down on corporate ripoffs, protecting families and honest businesses alike. The Mamdani administration’s work to tackle the affordability crisis and promote economic fairness continues to set a new standard nationwide, modeling effective governance and a relentless focus on using all of the city’s levers to improve life for New Yorkers. ”“New Yorkers across the five boroughs are feeling the squeeze of the affordability crisis as they pay more and more for less and less. Junk fees and subscription traps add to this, costing families an average of $3,200 per year. Big companies can’t play by their own rules, charging customers for things they don’t want or need. I applaud Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Deputy Mayor Julie Su and Commissioner Sam Levine for taking action to stop these exploitative business practices and lower costs for everyday New Yorkers,” said State Senator Kristen Gonzalez.
Article Summary: New York will become the first city in the US to require that consumers be allowed to cancel subscriptions for streaming services, gym memberships and more in the way that they signed up. FTC's ex-chairman Lina Khan commended Mamdani for the same.

Article Title: How Bees helped engineers solve the flaw regarded as Solar panels’ biggest shortcoming since their invention
Article Text:
Honeycomb geometry ‘helped’solve solar panel’s biggest shortcoming

Significant gains in solar panel efficiency

Potential applications beyond rooftops

Engineers have reportedly developed a new solar panel design inspired by the hexagonal honeycomb built by bees, offering a potential solution to one of the technology's biggest limitations. Conventional solar panels lose a significant amount of energy when sunlight strikes them at an angle, as much of the light is reflected away instead of being absorbed. As reported by The Pulse, the newly developed three-dimensional concave structure redirects reflected light back into the panel, allowing it to be captured. Researchers say the bee-inspired design could significantly improve solar panel efficiency without the need for expensive sun-tracking systems.Traditional solar panels are flat and generate the most electricity when sunlight falls directly on their surface around midday. As the sun moves across the sky, its rays hit the panels at increasingly oblique angles, causing more light to reflect off the protective glass.To overcome this, engineers replaced the flat architecture with a concave 3D design made using flexible mechanical metamaterials. The structure allows reflected light to bounce between angled surfaces inside the panel instead of escaping back into the atmosphere.This process, known as enhanced light recapture, gives the panel another opportunity to absorb the energy.According to researchers, the new design delivered a maximum power output increase of 142.3% compared with a conventional flat panel under the same conditions.At a zero-degree angle, where sunlight falls directly on the panel, power output increased by 36.4%. At a 60-degree angle, where traditional solar panels experience some of their highest reflection losses, performance improved by 61.8%.The design is based on the natural honey comb structure created by bees which gives maximum strength with a minimum of material. The engineers translated this geometry into micro-valleys that help trap and redirect incoming light.Because the supporting metamaterial is flexible, the technology could be integrated into curved building surfaces, electric vehicles and aerospace equipment, expanding the range of applications for solar power beyond conventional rooftop installations.
Article Summary: Conventional solar panels lose a significant amount of energy when sunlight strikes them at an angle. Three-dimensional concave structure redirects reflected light back into the panel, allowing it to be captured. Researchers say the bee-inspired design could significantly improve solar panel efficiency without the need for expensive sun-tracking systems.

Article Title: Apple releases public beta for iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, iPadOS 27, and more OS'
Article Text:
Apple's OS 27 public betas are out now.

Siri AI is the reason anyone is installing this beta

iOS 27 speed gains and a Liquid Glass slider for everyone else

What macOS Golden Gate , watchOS 27 and iPadOS 27 add

Siri AI is no longer something you have to take Apple 's word for. The company has released the public betas for its OS 27 lineup, which means anyone with an Apple ID can now install the rebuilt assistant that was announced, delayed, mocked, and re-announced over the better part of two years. No developer account needed. Just a sign-up page and a device you're willing to gamble on.The release covers iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, watchOS 27, tvOS 27 and visionOS 27. The builds are based on developer Beta 3, which shipped on July 3, with iPadOS and macOS getting a slightly newer revision. The finished software lands in the fall. Until then, this is Apple asking the public to poke holes in it—worth remembering before you put it on the phone you use for work.The new Siri does something the old one never managed: it remembers what you just said. Ask it to dig out a flight confirmation buried in Mail, then ask a follow-up without repeating yourself, and it holds the thread. It reads what's on your screen. It takes multi-step actions inside apps. And it can search your messages, photos, notes and calendar—the pitch being that an assistant with private access to your life beats one without.Then come the asterisks. You need an iPhone 15 Pro or newer. It speaks English only. It isn't launching in the EU. And there's a waitlist: Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri > Try New Siri, then wait for the notification. Developer beta testers reported waits stretching close to two weeks, though some public beta users are getting in within the hour.If the AI leaves you cold, iOS 27 still has a case to make. Apple says apps launch up to 30 percent faster, AirDrop moves files up to 80 percent quicker, and new shots appear in Photos up to 70 percent sooner. The CPU scheduler work reaches back to the iPhone 11, so this isn't a treat reserved for new hardware. Your phone should also stop clinging to a dead Wi-Fi signal on your way out the door.Liquid Glass, last year's most argued-about change, now has a slider under Settings > Appearance—drag it from glassy to solid. Safari groups tabs on its own and builds extensions from plain-English requests. Photos adds Extend and Spatial Reframing. The Passwords app quietly swaps out weak passwords. AirPods get a custom EQ, finally.On the Mac, Golden Gate sells Siri as a work tool. Summon it from Spotlight, point it at what's on screen, lean on it for writing. The design changes are quieter: uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, cleaner menu bar icons.watchOS 27 puts Siri on your wrist, which is arguably where a voice assistant makes most sense. A Dynamic App Grid surfaces what you're likely to need. Workout Buddy now runs without an iPhone nearby.iPadOS 27 inherits the iPhone features and adds little of its own, bar two things: Visual Intelligence works with the Apple Pencil—circle something to ask about it—and external SSD transfers are up to five times faster.To install, enrol at Apple's Beta Software Program page, then head to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates and pick the 27 public beta for your device. Back up first.
Article Summary: Apple's OS 27 public betas are out now. Anyone with an Apple ID can now install the rebuilt assistant that was announced, delayed, mocked, and re-announced over the better part of two years. Apple says apps launch up to 30 percent faster, AirDrop moves files up to 80 percent quicker, and new shots appear in Photos 70 percent sooner.

Article Title: Hack of the day: Track your passport dispatch and speed post delivery online
Article Text:
Start with Passport Seva



Then switch to India Post



What to do if the status seems stuck



One thing to keep in mind



There is a particular kind of anxiety that comes with waiting for a passport. You have done everything right — submitted the application, attended the appointment, cleared the police verification — and then the waiting begins. Days pass. Sometimes weeks. And at some point the question shifts from "when will it be approved" to "where on earth is it right now." The frustrating part is that the answer is almost always available online, and most people simply do not know where to look. Here is how to find out exactly where your passport is, from the moment it leaves the printing facility to the day it lands at your door.The first place to check is the official Passport Seva portal, which is where your application's status lives from start to finish. Open passportindia.gov.in and look for the Track Application Status option on the homepage. You do not need to log in for this. Select whether you applied for a passport or a Police Clearance Certificate, enter your file number exactly as it appears on your acknowledgement receipt, and enter your date of birth. The file number is the one that was given to you when you submitted your application, and it needs to be entered precisely, including any slashes or reference characters, because even a small variation will return no result.Once the status loads, work through what it says carefully. If your passport has been printed and dispatched, the status will typically say something along the lines of "Passport Dispatched" and will include a Speed Post tracking number. That number is what you need for the next step. Write it down or copy it before you move on.Once you have got your Speed Post number just go to indiapost.gov.in and use the Track and Trace tool to follow the package's movement through the postal network. Just key in your Speed Post number and the system will then show you a complete log of every location the consignment has passed along with the proper timestamps of each and every movement. The log will help you to identify whether the package is still at the regional sorting facility or it has reached the local post office near your address. The log will also tell you that if delivery was attempted and you were not at home. The tracking tool of India Post updates in real time as the consignment moves through the system, so refreshing it regularly gives you a reliable picture of how quickly things are progressing toward your address.Speed Post for passports can sometimes sit at a sorting hub for a day or two without visible movement, which looks alarming but is usually a routine part of the sorting process rather than a sign that something has gone wrong. Give it two to three working days before escalating. If movement genuinely stops for longer than that, the best next step is to call your local post office directly with the Speed Post number in hand, as they can check whether the package is physically present at the facility even if the online tracker has not updated.If the Passport Seva portal shows your passport as dispatched but you cannot find a Speed Post number in the status details, log into your Passport Seva account fully and check the status there, as the tracking number sometimes appears only in the logged-in view rather than the public tracking page.Delivery of passports is done by the post office, and if you are not available to receive it in person, the postman will leave a delivery notice and attempt re-delivery. Passports are treated as registered articles and require a signature, which means they will not be left with a neighbour or tucked under a doormat. If re-delivery is also missed, the package returns to the post office and is held there for a set number of days before being sent back to the passport office.Tracking regularly from the day your Passport Seva status shows dispatched means you will always know when to be available, and avoids the unnecessary complication of a returned consignment.
Article Summary: Tracking regularly from the day your Passport Seva status shows dispatched means you will always know when to be available. The tracking tool of India Post updates in real time as the consignment moves through the system, so refreshing it regularly gives you a reliable picture of how quickly things are progressing.

Article Title: Read the letter Eric Schmidt, Reid Hoffman, and top economists signed about AI wiping away millions of jobs; send a warning: Economists, policymakers and technology leaders must act now to understand
Article Text:
Who all have signed the letter



What the letter says



Over 200 of the world’s most influential economists, technology executives and researchers have signed an open letter warning that artificial intelligence (AI) poses a serious and growing threat to jobs. The letter also says that the governments are not moving fast enough to prepare for what is coming. The letter, titled “We Must Act Now” and subtitled “A Statement on AI's Transformation of the Economy”, was organised by the Stanford Digital Economy Lab. At just 88 words, it is deliberately concise.Among those who signed: former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, and Nobel Prize laureates Joseph Stiglitz, Daron Acemoglu, and Simon Johnson. Also on the list are Google AI lead Jeff Dean, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark and OpenAI finance chief Sarah Friar — making it one of the rare documents that brings together both AI builders and the economists studying the technology's consequences. Other include Godfathers of AI Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun, and Vinod Khosla.The letter’s argument is straightforward: It warns that AI could become “radically more powerful” over the coming decade, and without meaningful action from policymakers, the result could be “large-scale job displacement” on a scale the world has not seen before.We Must Act NowA Statement on AI’s Transformation of the EconomyAI may become radically more powerful over the next 10 years.This could drive an unprecedented transformation of our economy, larger than the Industrial Revolution, but unfolding over a vastly shorter time frame. It could bring risks, including large-scale job displacement, as well as opportunities such as major gains in living standards.Economists, policymakers and technology leaders must act now to understand the economics of transformative AI and to build the incentives, guardrails, and institutions needed to steer AI in a direction that complements humans and benefits society.The letter comes as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has predicted that AI could eliminate up to half of all entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. Many economists and technologists sit somewhere in between, arguing that AI is more likely to transform jobs than replace them outright.
Article Summary: Eric Schmidt, Reid Hoffman, Joseph Stiglitz, Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson, Jeff Dean, Sarah Friar, Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun all sign letter. Letter was organised by the Stanford Digital Economy Lab.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs’ widow Laurene Powell Jobs: "To do what you wanna do, to leave a mark, in a way that…" - a life well-lived is measured by what we leave behind
Article Text:
Laurene Powell Jobs (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Laurene Powell Jobs

"To do what you wanna do, to leave a mark, in a way that you think is important and lasting, that's a life well-lived"

The deeper meaning of Laurene Powell Jobs’ quote

Where this reflection actually comes from

Why lasting impact has defined her own work since

A meaningful legacy is rarely built overnight

Personal success becomes richer when it benefits others

Other memorable quotes by Laurene Powell Jobs

"Regardless of zip code, talent and IQ are evenly distributed, so we need to make sure that opportunity is evenly distributed, too."

"Broken institutions are an opportunity rather than a time to go home."

"The innovation and creativity that's so manifest in the rest of society needs to be turned on our school systems."

"Whether someone signs something is not what's important. It's what they do and how they do it that matters."

Why this timeless message still resonates

Most people want their life to add up to more than a list of achievements. Laurene Powell Jobs put that idea into one sentence: "To do what you wanna do, to leave a mark, in a way that you think is important and lasting, that's a life well-lived. " It is a simple way of separating a full life from a merely busy one, built around what actually lasts rather than what looks impressive in the moment. The words are plain, almost conversational, yet they draw a clear line between chasing recognition and building something that continues to matter once the attention has moved on. It is the kind of definition that works just as well for a teacher or a small business owner as it does for anyone running a large philanthropic organisation.The quote opens with authenticity. Doing what you actually want to do, rather than following expectations set by someone else, is presented as the starting point, not an optional extra. Purpose cannot simply be copied from someone else's definition of success.The "mark" she describes is deliberately left open. It is not defined by wealth or fame. It could be a school, an idea, a piece of writing, or simply a life that quietly made things better for the people around it.The final phrase, "that's a life well-lived," shifts the whole measurement away from visibility and toward whether something genuinely lasting was actually built.Powell Jobs gave this interview only months after Steve Jobs ' death in October 2011, at a moment when a great deal of public attention was focused on his legacy specifically. Rather than talking only about her late husband's achievements, she used the interview to describe her own view of what makes a life meaningful, a definition built around lasting contribution rather than public recognition.That context matters. She was not offering a detached philosophy. She was speaking from inside a very public, very recent experience of watching someone's life get measured and remeasured by the world after it ended.Powell Jobs founded Emerson Collective, an organisation that blends philanthropy with policy work and investment across education, immigration and journalism, rather than operating as a conventional grant-making foundation. She has spoken about wanting talent and opportunity distributed as evenly as intelligence already is, and has described broken institutions as something worth rebuilding rather than abandoning.That approach mirrors the quote closely. Rather than chasing quick, visible wins, her work has consistently focused on slower, structural change in education and immigration policy, the kind of contribution that takes years to show results and rarely produces an immediate headline.Modern culture tends to celebrate sudden success, viral moments and instant recognition, which can create the impression that meaningful achievement happens quickly. Most lasting contributions do not work that way. Institutions, research and community change all tend to accumulate slowly, through effort that rarely draws attention while it is actually happening.What stands out in the quote is its outward focus. It is not simply about achieving something for yourself. It is about creating something that continues to matter to other people once your own involvement in it has ended, which turns individual ambition into something with a longer shelf life than personal achievement alone usually has.In a culture that constantly measures, compares and shares achievement, Powell Jobs' quote is a reminder that the value of a life rarely comes down to any of that. What tends to last is whatever was actually built for other people to use, long after the person who built it has moved on to something else.
